title: Scalarize balanced two-source trace entropy with a testing curve
statement: For two faithful positive matrices A,X on one finite-dimensional space, mu=(Tr(A-tX)_+)'' is a finite positive measure with h(t)=integral(r-t)_+mu(dr), integral mu=TrX, and integral r mu=TrA. It matches positive and negative trace parts for every real pencil alpha A+beta X. Both coefficient balances then give the exact entropy integral; scalar validity is equivalent, and singular inputs follow by positive regularization and continuity.

requires: Two faithful positive operators A,X on the same finite-dimensional space, nonnegative mixture coefficients alpha_j,beta_j, and both sums sum_j c_j alpha_j=sum_j c_j beta_j=0.
provides: An abstract positive testing-curve measure reproducing all real binary pencil positive/negative traces and an exact scalar representation of balanced mixture entropy; scalar inequalities lift iff they hold for all nonnegative scalar pairs.
assumptions: A and X need not commute. The faithful h'(0+) argument uses full support; singular matrices are handled only by A+epsilon I,X+epsilon I and entropy continuity, with endpoint atoms accounted for.
costs: Exact finite-dimensional identities in nats; matrix dimension and numerical precision have no supplied algorithmic or physical cost.
contract.units: Natural-log entropy in nats; mu is a finite positive measure, not a probability measure unless normalized and not an acquired experiment.
contract.obstruction: No universal extension to three or more independent sources, unbalanced entropy combinations, arbitrary products, partial transposes, or general matrix-valued functional calculus.

evidence.quote:
For Y=alpha A+beta X and Z=gamma A+delta X with nonnegative coefficients and
nonzero mixtures, Frenkel Theorem6 expresses Umegaki D(Y||Z) as Tr(Y-Z) plus a
positive integral of the negative trace of (1-t)Y+tZ. Every such pencil has the
same positive/negative trace as its classical counterpart, hence
D(Y||Z)=integral (alpha r+beta) log[(alpha r+beta)/(gamma r+delta)] mu(dr).
The trace term is essential for unequal traces and is matched by the moments.
Classical interchange of the nonnegative integral follows by Tonelli. Faithful
finite source matrices keep r in a compact positive interval.

Primary source, actually read: P. E. Frenkel, Integral formula for quantum
relative entropy implies data processing inequality, arXiv:2208.12194v4,
Theorem6, https://arxiv.org/html/2208.12194 . The theorem explicitly allows
positive semidefinite matrices with unequal traces. It is not a statement that
quantum experiments are physically classical.

body:
1. Set h(t)=Tr(A-tX)_+. Faithfulness makes h affine near zero and identically zero for all sufficiently large t; its distributional second derivative mu is positive with compact support in (0,infinity). Integrating twice from infinity gives h(t)=integral(r-t)_+mu(dr); the value and right derivative at zero give integral r mu=TrA and integral mu=TrX.
2. If alpha,beta have opposite signs, scale h(t) with t the ratio of the negative to positive coefficient. For equal signs the pencil has one sign. The trace identity TrY_+-TrY_-=TrY gives both positive and negative scalar-pencil trace matches.
3. Apply Frenkel Theorem 6 to two nonzero positive mixtures Y and Z. Every pencil (1-t)Y+tZ remains a real combination of A,X, so its positive/negative trace is matched by the scalar densities alpha r+beta and gamma r+delta. The trace term for unequal traces is matched by the two moments.
4. Write each balanced entropy sum as -sum_j c_j D(Y_j||A+X). Both balance equations make sum_j c_jY_j=0, cancelling the operator reference-log term; the scalar reference log(r+1) cancels for the same reason. The remaining integral is exactly the scalar entropy combination.
5. Integrate any scalar inequality against mu, using the moments for optional linear trace terms; the one-dimensional case proves necessity. Approximate singular matrices by A+epsilon I,X+epsilon I and take the entropy-continuity limit.
